title: Raleigh
content: Prior to the experience, my grandmother appeared to be beating a dog to death. I intervened and yelled at her to stop. She rushed at me, grabbed me by the neck, and we tripped over a dog gate in the process. I lost consciousness when my head hit the carpeted, concrete floor. I experienced a vast darkness and an intense pleasure, unlike anything I had ever felt - including from opioids. I felt warm but bodiless. There was a sense of formlessness and space. I felt my mind fading away into nothingness and found it hard not to give in. I somehow found the strength to escape it by thinking about my mother, whom I loved very much. I regained consciousness, gasping for breath. My grandmother was frantically beating my chest. She told me to get up and stop being so dramatic. I lay there for a long time, and she tried to drag me up the stairs to my room. I stayed at the foot of the stairs until my mom came home. My grandmother had gone to her room by then. I did not care about anything and felt like nothing mattered. I did not even tell my mom what happened. My grandmother lied and my mother was angry at me, which was shocking. I eventually moved away, but I have felt very numb much of the time, ever since that moment. Otherwise, I have been depressed or panic-stricken. Sometimes I am happy.

elements.At the time of your experience, was ther: Yes, Criminal attack, Direct head injury, Life threatening event, but not clinical death
elements.Did you feel separated from your body?: I clearly left my body and existed outside it
elements.How did your highest level of consciousn: Less consciousness and alertness than normal
elements.Did time seem to speed up or slow down?: Everything seemed to be happening at once; or time stopped or lost all meaning, Time was meaningless, but I felt things.
elements.Please compare your vision during the ex: I felt like I was formless, except for a mind. Everything was black, but not like looking at the backs of your eyelids in the pitch black dark. It was like light had never been there. There was no ambient light of any kind.
elements.Did you see an unearthly light?: Uncertain, I have a vague recollection of a pin of light when I became frightened, but I'm not sure. I don't remember that part clearly. It could have just been my vision being restored as I regained consciousness.
elements.Did you seem to enter some other, uneart: A clearly mystical or unearthly realm, A black void.
elements.Did you come to a border or point of no: I came to a definite conscious decision to return to life, I believe I remembered or thought of my mother, without words. I felt like I couldn't hurt her by dying, so I resisted the feelings of pleasure and comfort.
elements.What was your religion prior to your exp: Unaffiliated- Nothing in particular- Secular unaffiliated
elements.What is your religion now?: Unaffiliated- Agnostic, I sometimes entertain that there is a god, but do not know. I am more philosophically inclined than religious.
elements.Did your experience include features con: Content that was entirely not consistent with the beliefs you had at the time of your experience, I don't know how to answer this because I was a child. But I don't think I believed in formlessness or void, nor that there could be comfort or pleasure in either.
elements.What life changes occurred in your life: I am educated in philosophy, so I argue about everything. I believe that likely has contributed more than my experience to my current worldviews. After my experience, up until my thyroid cancer started affecting my health, I was intensely atheistic and nihilistic. Thyroid cancer wrecked my mental health and I became monotheistic. Then I found philosophy and the changes above happened.
elements.Have your relationships changed specific: Uncertain, It happened at a young age. I don’t remember enough about prior to that.
elements.How accurately do you remember the exper: I remember the experience more accurately than other life events that occurred around the time of the experience, I was a child, but I have a well-defined vision of what happened, as with many of my other traumas. I can remember clearly what happened prior to, after, and during the event.
elements.What did you believe about the reality o: Experience was definitely real, I don’t remember, truthfully. I didn’t feel anything. I didn’t believe anything.
elements.What do you believe about the reality of: Experience was definitely real, It was at least real in that it was an experience, a perception, not necessarily in that a void is a place, or that nothing is real.
elements.Did the questions asked and information: Uncertain, There is a lack of belief that has resulted, and an unwavering uncertainty in everything. I don’t believe that uncertainty or disbelief has been quantified in the questions.
